record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.context_brief: CF-MMIMO with RIS, near-field, and AI
record.original_question: How should cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO) be combined with other advanced 6G technologies, including reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, near-field transmissions, and artificial-intelligence methods, while preserving scalable channel estimation, scheduling, synchronization, signal processing, and resource allocation in ultra-dense deployments?

evidence.quote: In addition to the key questions addressed in this paper, there are still many interesting research questions requiring future comprehensive studies, such as 1) At what level of densification is CF-MMIMO truly beneficial? When is it not really needed?; 2) How to handle high mobility in UDNs with CF-MMIMO?; 3) CF-MMIMO for communication with backscattering devices; 4) How CF-MMIMO works (including channel estimation, scheduling procedures, signal processing at the users) with multiple-antenna users; and 5) How to combine CF-MMIMO with other advanced technologies such as reconfigurable intelligent surface, near-field transmissions, and AI technologies.
Furthermore, 6G is poised to enable new use cases stemming from advanced capabilities, particularly those related to artificial intelligence (AI) and multi-sensory interactions.
Importantly, RadioWeaves, and CF-MMIMO more generally, naturally operates in the [geometric] near-field of the “super-array” collectively constituted by all antenna panels together.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an ultra-dense wireless deployment modeled as cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO): a large set of geographically distributed access points (APs), each equipped with multiple antennas and connected via fronthaul links to one or more central processing units, jointly and coherently serve a much smaller number of single- or multi-antenna user equipments (UEs) on the same time-frequency resources, without forming traditional cells. Let the wireless channel between AP m and UE k be a vector h_{mk} ∈ C^{N_m} that must be estimated from uplink pilots of finite length τ_p, and let scheduling, synchronization across APs, signal processing, and radio-resource allocation be carried out by algorithms whose per-UE computational and fronthaul complexity must remain bounded as the number of APs M and UEs K grow (the scalability requirement).

Augment this baseline with three additional components:
(i) Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs): passive planar arrays of N_R reflecting elements whose per-element phase shifts θ_n ∈ [0, 2π) can be programmed to reshape the propagation channel, so that h_{mk} = h_{mk}^{(d)} + G_m Φ f_k where Φ = diag(e^{jθ_1},…,e^{jθ_{N_R}}) and G_m, f_k are AP-RIS and RIS-UE channels.
(ii) Near-field transmissions: when UEs or scatterers lie within the Fraunhofer distance of the collective aperture formed by all APs, the planar-wave model fails and channels must be described by spherical-wave models depending on both angle and distance, so beamforming and channel estimation operate in a higher-dimensional angle-distance domain.
(iii) Artificial-intelligence methods: data-driven models (e.g., deep neural networks, reinforcement-learning agents) used in place of or alongside model-based algorithms for one or more of channel estimation, precoder/combiner design, user-AP association, pilot assignment, and power control.

Problem. Design joint protocols and algorithms for such a CF-MMIMO system that simultaneously incorporate RISs, near-field propagation, and AI-based processing, such that the following scalability and performance criteria all hold as M, K, N_R → ∞ with K/M and N_R/M bounded:
(a) the per-UE pilot overhead, channel-estimation computational cost, and fronthaul signaling per coherence block remain O(1);
(b) the scheduling, synchronization, and resource-allocation procedures admit distributed implementations with bounded per-AP complexity and bounded information exchange between APs;
(c) the achieved per-user spectral efficiency is no worse, up to a vanishing additive term, than that of a fully centralized, fully informed benchmark that jointly optimizes RIS phases, near-field beamforming, and power allocation under perfect channel state information.

Provide such a construction, or prove that no scheme satisfying (a)–(c) exists, and characterize the fundamental trade-offs among densification level, mobility, channel-state-information quality, RIS configuration overhead, near-field aperture size, and AI model complexity that govern when these joint designs are beneficial.
artifact.status_search_result: The integration of cell-free massive MIMO with RIS, near-field propagation, and AI under scalability constraints is widely identified as an open research direction in 6G wireless surveys and ongoing research from 2023–2026. No comprehensive solution satisfying the scalability and optimality criteria has been reported; only partial results addressing isolated subproblems (e.g., RIS-aided CF-MMIMO channel estimation, near-field beamforming, or AI-based power control) are available.

status_evidence.title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
status_evidence.snippet: Lists combining CF-MMIMO with RIS, near-field transmissions, and AI as open research questions requiring future comprehensive studies.
status_evidence.claim: The joint integration question is posed as open.

status_evidence.title: Recent surveys on RIS-aided cell-free MIMO and near-field communications
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent works address isolated aspects (RIS-aided CF-MMIMO, near-field beamforming, AI-based resource allocation) but do not provide a unified scalable framework.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial progress on subproblems has been reported.
